title: Belafonte's show with Hank Jones on piano and Harry's free hand
summary: Duke did not need to play because Hank Jones was on the track; Belafonte gave Jones latitude and he hired outside heavyweights.

story.theme_name: Jazz musicians in the movies and film scoring
story.community_name: Jazz musicians on film and studio scoring

blocks.x: Yeah. But I was speaking about that. I think we talked about that.

And Duke didn't have to play, because there was Hank Jones in there playing. I had to put all that stuff together. But Harry gave me so much latitude. The only hard thing about it was just staying up around the clock. But all the other problems were out of the way. No political overtones or anything.

You know. And, oh, I did some research. Lou Shubie (PHONETIC), who's the CBS contractor back there, when they were using studio bands, I would go and check the bands playing in the studios, and I told Harry, I said, 'We'll have to come outside and get the big heavyweights.' And he said, 'Man, do what you want to do. I've got it straight with the network.' And the music turned out that way, you know?
